stats.fact: PromptShield (jovial-liu) is a local-first static scanner: no model, API key, upload, or dependency required; runs fully offline and produces SARIF 2.1.0 output.

PromptShield ships 6 detection rules: prompt-injection (high), secret-exfiltration (high), dangerous-pipeline (medium), approval-bypass (medium), encoded-instruction (medium), hidden-unicode (medium).

PromptShield scans 20+ text extensions (.md, .mdx, .txt, .yml, .yaml, .json, .toml, .ini, .sh, .bash, .zsh, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .tsx, .py, .go, .rs, .java, .rb, .php, .html, .xml) and skips .git, node_modules, vendor, dist, build, coverage, .next, .cache.
PromptShield enforces per-file 500KB and 2000-file scan limits, and supports .promptshieldignore plus repeatable --exclude for intentional security fixtures.
PromptShield's --strict flag exits 1 when any non-info finding exists, enabling it as a CI gate; the GitHub Action runs locally on the runner and can upload SARIF to Code Scanning.
PromptShield is MIT-licensed, JavaScript/Node >=18, currently v0.2.0 (added .promptshieldignore and --exclude filters), created 2026-08-19.

Hidden/bidirectional Unicode (U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060, U+2066-U+2069, U+FEFF) can hide instructions from human reviewers while AI agents still process them — the core attack PromptShield's hidden-unicode rule targets.
The prompt-injection rule flags 'ignore/disregard/override previous instructions', 'system/developer prompt', 'reveal hidden/system/developer prompt', and 'do not tell/show the user' patterns.

angles: Local-first, zero-dependency static scanning is the key differentiator vs model-based or cloud scanners — no data leaves the repo, no API cost, works in air-gapped CI
Explainable findings: each rule is a readable regex pointing to file+line, framed as a 'review prompt' not proof of malicious intent — reduces false-positive fatigue
Hidden Unicode is the invisible threat: bidirectional and zero-width controls pass human diff review but are read by agents — PromptShield catches what reviewers cannot see
CI-native design: GitHub Action + SARIF 2.1.0 + --strict gate makes it a drop-in Code Scanning integration for agent-heavy repos
Supply-chain angle: as AI coding agents auto-read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules/skills, scanning repos before an agent touches them becomes a security baseline
Rule coverage is deliberately narrow and readable, with a documented false-positive posture (generated docs, test fixtures, security training may match intentionally)
